rv.q: Younger’s consistently clever plotting links the events of the past to the present without things feeling overly ham-fisted.

Los Feliz’s Skylight Theatre has been a shining light among L.A. stages for going on a half-century, and if Rorschach is any indication of what lies ahead, theatergoing Angelinos are in for even more greatness in the months and years ahead.
Every part of this show exudes incredible attention to detail, making for a wonderful experience exploring not just an inkblot test but a world of colorful emotions.
The desire to be fully seen is at the heart of the play, and the characters become so through a generous script that gives them all nuance and clarity, as well as pitch-perfect casting and acting.
The ensemble, and the tech designers deliver an enticing production that mines Younger’s humor and pathos with equal assurance.

Younger’s writing shines brightest in the dialogue, especially unexpected moments of witty repartee (“Did you say hence ?”) among the modern characters, and in weaving the play’s disparate strands to a satisfying conclusion.
A funny, inventive, and surprisingly tender new play about the art and science of perception, the courage to be seen for who we truly are, and the mysterious, blotted shape of love itself.

Rorschach has all the raw visual tools and a few brilliant performances to make for an engaging evening, but until the dialogue stops leaning on stagecraft, the emotional picture remains out of focus.

cn.t: Critics mostly embrace *Rorschach*'s inventive, tender premise—weaving romance and psychology through inkblot-inspired storytelling—with strong performances winning praise. A few find it uneven, but its whimsical originality earns a warm, if not unanimous, reception.
